clip.role: identifies both voices, and documents which tag is which dataset speaker

speakers.line: Did you end up going to that new café near campus?
Yeah, I went yesterday after class. It was actually pretty nice.

mapping_warning: S1 and S2 run opposite to the dataset's A and B. S1 is aKw9UnnjRq5scbeeGI7Z, which make_audio.py assigns to speaker B; S2 is s3TPKV1kjDlVtZbl4Ksh, which it assigns to speaker A. Wiring a cloning renderer S1->A and S2->B would swap the voices against the ElevenLabs renders, and every metric splits by renderer, so the difference would look like a renderer effect.

clone_from.role: the timbre a cloning renderer should reproduce
clone_from.why_only_one_voice_is_needed: Dia supplies only the gasp and groan clips, and the vocalization is always produced by the speaker of turn 5 — speaker A in every item, since the turns run A-B-A-B-A. So a cloning renderer never needs speaker B's voice.
unconfirmed: Which dataset speaker this is. Speaker A (s3TPKV1kjDlVtZbl4Ksh) is the inference, because A produces every vocalization, but it is not stated and has not been checked by listening.
What is said in it. Dia conditions on a reference recording together with its transcript, so this is left null rather than guessed — the same gap the previous Dia reference had.
